questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I primarily went on exchange to have fun and to improve my spanish language skills.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it was in spain, because i wanted to improve my spanish.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a great stay, but the clinical rotations where really boring and the proces of going on exchange was really exhausting.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: When i arrived, it was more or less easy to figure out what to do. But you need to have in mind that nothing is really structured in spain, but just go with the flow.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't really receive any help. There is a coordinator at the hospital that will help you out a little bit, but only if you contact her yourself i think.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: There isnt any on campus housing. And it was actually quite difficult to find housing. I used idealiste, and lived with the other Medical student from KU. But we had a really hard time finding an appartment, no one wanted to lent out their appartment for less than 5 months. So we ended up having to rent for 5 months, even thoug we only stayed for 3 1/2.  But it is quite cheap.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Live in La Arena in Gijon! great place to stay! you are close to the beach, the hospital and everything important in the city. And use idealista or the erasmus chat to find housing.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Well everything has just been one big mess

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Nothing really

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Well when you arrive it is easy to change the rotations you want to do, even though you planned something else, and you can more or less choose whatever you want.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have faith in the process and be proactive. Write the hospital and the erasmus coordinatior at Uni Ovi yourself.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The clinical rotations are quite boring, you dont really get to do much. But depends a lot on the doctors i guess.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: You just do clinical rotations

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Well it is only clinical rotations. But you dont get to do as much as you would in DK

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Clinical rotations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Endocrinology was nice, because they where really sweet. If you like surgery, i think most of the surgical fields are nice, because you get to scrub in. If you dont like surgery (like me) you end up being really bored.

questions.answer: You just use a lot of money going on trips, but is so nice! and you should definetly do it. And really just enjoy student life!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: well food is not that much cheaper than at home. But coffee and going out i cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The erasmus community in Oviedo/Gijon is really active. I joined a lot in the beginning, and found some really nice friends, that i did things with. And i would definetly recomend going to Oviedo, because there is a lot of Erasmus students there, and a lot of medical students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of things arranged by erasmus.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend going to as many events as you can in the first few weeks, and dont be afraid to go talk to people. And then i would recommend going to picos de europa and do some hiking, really beautiful!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Picos!! You can rent cheap cars with Budget/Avis, so rent a car and drive somewhere. The west coast is nice, the east coast is nice, Madrid is nice. Go hiking near Somiedo / behind Oviedo - you can take the bus and do day trips. f.eks. Ojo de Buye

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: There is no lunch break at the hospital, but just leave early.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is difficult, but i meet a few at the hospital.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Its just tirring to talk spanish all the time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Siesta.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Have faith in the process, thing will work out when you arrive. Enjoy student life, and have a lot of fun!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Figure out if there is another one from KU going, it makes it so much easier. And reach out to previous students.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Everything outside the hospital.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being at the hospital, speaking Spanish

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: You will be going to the hospital in Gijon called Cabueñes.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
